analysis.text:
The image is a choropleth map of Karnataka districts in India, displaying the Gross District Domestic Product (GDDP) in ₹ Crore. The map uses a color gradient to represent the GDDP, with darker shades indicating higher GDDP values and lighter shades indicating lower GDDP values. The legend on the right side of the map shows the GDDP ranges, with the darkest shade representing GDDP values of 1,00,000+ and the lightest shade representing GDDP values of 20,000 or less.

The map includes the names of all the districts in Karnataka, with the most populous and economically developed districts, such as Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, and Mysuru, shaded in dark red, indicating the highest GDDP values. Other districts are shaded in varying shades of orange and yellow, representing lower GDDP values.

The source of the data is the Department of Economics & Statistics, Government of Karnataka (2023-24). The map also includes a north indicator at the bottom left corner.
